title: BoundedScalarConvex.lean

problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize a convex, H-Lipschitz function on the nonempty closed interval [lower, upper] in ℝ. A minimizer xstar exists with |x0−xstar|≤R. No differentiability or strong convexity is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: A stochastic subgradient oracle returns a scalar G_n at an adapted feasible query x_n. Almost surely |G_n|≤H, and E[G_n | past_n] supports f throughout the feasible interval. Function values and exact subgradients are not supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The almost-sure reply bound implies E[G_n² | past_n]≤H² and E[(G_n−E[G_n | past_n])² | past_n]≤H².

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The decision space is one-dimensional Euclidean space ℝ, with absolute-value distance.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: The joint seed law may have arbitrary temporal dependence; neither independence nor mixing is assumed. Conditional subgradient validity is required for every past-measurable feasible query. All parameters lower, upper, H>0, R≥0, ε>0, and feasible x0 are public; f and the oracle law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BoundedScalarConvex.lean: past, IsBoundedSubgradientOracle, Params, spec.Public, spec.publicInput, and spec.valid; LongTails/Template.lean: Oracle.law.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The output has an integrable objective gap f(output)−f(xstar), whose expectation is at most ε for an interval minimizer xstar.

accuracy.label: feasibility
accuracy.details: The output must be measurable and belong to [lower, upper] for every realization.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: The guarantee averages over algorithm randomness and the joint oracle seed law. Oracle cost is bounded by the fixed extracted budget max(1, ceil(25H²R²/ε²)) on every execution.
accuracy.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BoundedScalarConvex.lean: spec.successful; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence and execute; supplied result budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Constrained Lipschitz convex minimization with bounded stochastic subgradient replies, conditional subgradient validity, and expected objective-gap accuracy is a standard stochastic approximation formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Bounded Scalar Convex Optimization

We consider minimizing a convex, H-Lipschitz function f:R→R on C=[a,b], where a≤b and H>0. A given point x0∈C lies within distance R≥0 of a minimizer x⋆∈C. The oracle returns a random scalar bounded in absolute value by H, whose conditional mean given past oracle randomness is a subgradient on C; replies may be dependent. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable, always feasible output x¯ with integrable objective gap and EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε, where P is the joint law of algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Cf(x). The algorithm receives a,b,H,R,ε, and x0, with the parameter ranges given above. Its randomness is independent of the oracle randomness.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and Lipschitz continuity). For every x,y∈C and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y),|f(x)−f(y)|≤H|x−y|.

Assumption 2 (Initial distance). There exists x⋆∈C such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈C,|x0−x⋆|≤R.

Assumption 3 (Bounded conditional subgradients). Let ξ=(ξn)n≥0 denote the oracle’s random samples with joint law ν, and let Fn=σ(ξ0,…,ξn−1). At call n, the scalar reply has the form Gn(h,x,ξn), where h∈(R×R)n is a history of query–reply pairs and x∈R is the query. For each n, the map Gn is jointly measurable in its history, query, and sample arguments.

For every Fn-measurable history hn and every Fn-measurable query Xn taking values in C for every realization, define gn=Gn(hn,Xn,ξn),sn=Eν[gn∣Fn]. These replies satisfy |gn|≤Hν-a.s.,f(Xn)+sn(y−Xn)≤f(y)for all y∈C,ν-a.s. The second inequality holds simultaneously for every y∈C outside a single null set for each choice of n,hn,Xn. The bound on gn ensures its integrability.

The oracle is defined for real queries; its boundedness and conditional subgradient guarantees apply to queries in C. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and belong to C for every realization. Its objective gap must be integrable under P and satisfy EP[f(x¯)−f(x⋆)]≤ε.

theorems.referencesHtml: • Angelia Nedić and Soomin Lee. On Stochastic Subgradient Mirror-Descent Algorithm with Weighted Averaging. 2014; consulted 2013 preprint v1. Complexity: O(1+D2(C2+ν2)/ε2) fixed stochastic subgradient calls for expected objective gap ≤ε, using Euclidean mirror descent with weighted averaging. Here D is the feasible-set diameter, C bounds mean subgradients, and ν2 bounds conditional error second moments; on [lower,upper]∩[x0−R,x0+R], D≤2R and C,ν≤H.
theorems.formulaHtml: max{1,⌈25⋅H2⋅R2ε2⌉+}

comparisonHtml:
Convex, H-Lipschitz f on C=[lower,upper]⊂R, with H>0, x0∈C, and a minimizer x⋆∈C satisfying |x0−x⋆|≤R, R≥0. Replies are jointly measurable in query and seed; at every query measurable with respect to the revealed-seed past Ft, |gt|≤H almost surely and EP[gt∣Ft]∈∂Cf(xt). No independence is assumed. Target: measurable xout∈C with integrable gap and ∫(f(xout)−f(x⋆))dP≤ε, ε>0. The setup imposes no algorithm restriction; (1) constructs constant-step projected SGD and returns its last iterate.

Comparison for BoundedScalarConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) BoundedScalarConvex (Ours) (review) O(1+H2R2/ε2)
(2) Linear-decay SGD (Liu and Zhou 2026, Thm. 3.4, v4) O(1+H2R2/ε2) (1): Matches known rate and last-iterate guarantee; constant-step analysis instead of linear decay. No parameter-knowledge gain. (1) requires scalar, compact domains and bounded replies; (2) allows arbitrary dimension, unbounded domains and finite-variance noise.
(3) Scheduled SGD (Jain et al. 2019, Thm. 1, full version) O(1+H2D2/ε2)
Independent-noise restriction.		 (1): R2 instead of D2; factor (D/R)2 when 0<R<D, ε≤HR. Allows adapted replies. (2) already removes diameter dependence. (1) is scalar; (3) allows arbitrary dimension.
(4) Constant-step scalar SGD (Beretta et al. 2026, Thm. 2, Eq. (2), v1) O(1+H2R2/ε2)
Bounded-reply overlap; additive, state-independent i.i.d. noise, L=H, σ≤H.		 (1): Matches rate; extends constant-step last-iterate analysis to bounded, history-, state- and time-dependent replies. (1) requires bounded replies and compact intervals; (4) permits unbounded finite-variance noise and unbounded intervals.

Abbr: Costs count stochastic-subgradient calls. D=upper−lower; P is the oracle trajectory law; ∂C denotes relative subgradients. In (4), L is the Lipschitz bound and σ2 bounds noise variance.

import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ConditionalExpectation.Basic

open MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.BoundedScalarConvex

open OracleTemplate

abbrev Samples (O : Oracle ℝ ℝ) := (k : ℕ) → O.Seed k

abbrev HistoryEntry := (Fin 1 × ℝ) × ℝ

abbrev HistoryAt (n : ℕ) := {history : List HistoryEntry // history.length = n}

def historyCoordinates (n : ℕ) (history : HistoryAt n) : Fin n → HistoryEntry :=
  fun i => history.val.getD i.val ((0, 0), 0)

@[instance_reducible]
instance historyAtMeasurableSpace (n : ℕ) : MeasurableSpace (HistoryAt n) :=
  MeasurableSpace.comap (historyCoordinates n) inferInstance

def answerAt (O : Oracle ℝ ℝ) (n : ℕ) (history : HistoryAt n)
    (query : Fin 1 × ℝ) (seed : O.Seed n) : ℝ :=
  O.answer history.val query (cast (congrArg O.Seed history.property.symm) seed)

@[instance_reducible]
def past (O : Oracle ℝ ℝ) (n : ℕ) : MeasurableSpace (Samples O) :=
  ⨆ k : Fin n, MeasurableSpace.comap (fun ω : Samples O => ω k)
    (inferInstance : MeasurableSpace (O.Seed k))

structure Params where
  lower : ℝ
  upper : ℝ
  H : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : ℝ

def IsBoundedSubgradientOracle (q : Params) (f : ℝ → ℝ) (O : Oracle ℝ ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ n, Measurable (fun z : (HistoryAt n × (Fin 1 × ℝ)) × O.Seed n =>
    answerAt O n z.1.1 z.1.2 z.2)) ∧
    ∀ n (history : Samples O → HistoryAt n) (x : Samples O → ℝ),
      Measurable[past O n] history → Measurable[past O n] x →
      (∀ ω, x ω ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper) →
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂(O.law : Measure _), |answerAt O n (history ω) (0, x ω) (ω n)| ≤ q.H) ∧
      (∀ᵐ ω ∂(O.law : Measure _), ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper,
        f (x ω) + ((O.law : Measure _)[fun ξ => answerAt O n (history ξ) (0, x ξ) (ξ n) | past O n]) ω *
          (y-x ω) ≤ f y)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance _ := ℝ → ℝ
  Query _ := ℝ
  Reply _ := ℝ
  Output _ := ℝ
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := q.lower ≤ q.upper ∧ 0 < q.H ∧ 0 ≤ q.R ∧ 0 < q.ε ∧
    q.x0 ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper
  admissible q f O :=
    ConvexOn ℝ (Set.Icc q.lower q.upper) f ∧
    (∀ x ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper, ∀ y ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper,
      |f x-f y| ≤ q.H*|x-y|) ∧
    (∃ xstar ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper,
      IsMinOn f (Set.Icc q.lower q.upper) xstar ∧ |q.x0-xstar| ≤ q.R) ∧
    IsBoundedSubgradientOracle q f O
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    (∀ ω, output ω ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper) ∧
    ∃ xstar ∈ Set.Icc q.lower q.upper, IsMinOn f (Set.Icc q.lower q.upper) xstar ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => f (output ω)-f xstar) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, f (output ω)-f xstar ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ q.ε

end LongTails.Setups.BoundedScalarConvex
